$comment: Monosai grammar catalog source. Authored for Monosai and dedicated to the public domain (CC0-1.0). JLPT does not publish an official exhaustive grammar list; `level` records where a pattern is conventionally taught. Built by scripts/assets/build-grammar-catalog.mjs.

rules.descriptionEn: Polite way of saying that something is something else.
rules.exampleJa: 私は学生です。
rules.exampleEn: I am a student.

rules.nameEn: ではありません (polite negative copula)
rules.descriptionEn: Polite way of saying that something is not the case.
rules.formation: Noun / na-adjective + ではありません
rules.exampleJa: 学生ではありません。
rules.exampleEn: I am not a student.

rules.descriptionEn: Plain-form statement that something is something else.
rules.exampleJa: これは本だ。
rules.exampleEn: This is a book.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks what the sentence is about and often sets up a contrast.
rules.exampleJa: 今日は暑いです。
rules.exampleEn: Today is hot.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the subject, especially new information or the subject of a descriptive clause.
rules.exampleJa: 猫がいます。
rules.exampleEn: There is a cat.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the thing an action is done to.
rules.exampleJa: 水を飲みます。
rules.exampleEn: I drink water.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a point in time, a destination, or the receiver of an action.
rules.exampleJa: 七時に起きます。
rules.exampleEn: I get up at seven.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the tool, method, or place where an action happens.
rules.exampleJa: バスで行きます。
rules.exampleEn: I go by bus.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the direction of movement, slightly more formal than に.
rules.exampleJa: 駅へ行きます。
rules.exampleEn: I go towards the station.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the start and end of a span of time or space.
rules.formation: Noun + から + noun + まで
rules.exampleJa: 九時から五時まで働きます。
rules.exampleEn: I work from nine to five.

rules.descriptionEn: Joins nouns exhaustively, or marks the person you do something with.
rules.exampleJa: 友だちと話します。
rules.exampleEn: I talk with a friend.

rules.descriptionEn: Says that the statement applies to this item as well.
rules.exampleJa: 私も行きます。
rules.exampleEn: I will go too.

rules.descriptionEn: Links two nouns, showing possession, origin, or description.
rules.exampleJa: 私の本です。
rules.exampleEn: It is my book.

rules.descriptionEn: Turns a statement into a question without changing word order.
rules.exampleJa: 行きますか。
rules.exampleEn: Are you going?

rules.descriptionEn: Polite non-past verb form for habits, facts, and future plans.
rules.exampleJa: 毎日読みます。
rules.exampleEn: I read every day.

rules.descriptionEn: Polite negative verb form for habits and refusals.
rules.exampleJa: 肉を食べません。
rules.exampleEn: I do not eat meat.

rules.descriptionEn: Polite past verb form for completed actions and past states.
rules.exampleJa: 映画を見ました。
rules.exampleEn: I watched a film.

rules.nameEn: ませんでした (polite past negative)
rules.descriptionEn: Polite past negative verb form.
rules.formation: Verb stem + ませんでした
rules.exampleJa: 行きませんでした。
rules.exampleEn: I did not go.

rules.descriptionEn: Suggests doing something together.
rules.exampleJa: 一緒に行きましょう。
rules.exampleEn: Let us go together.

rules.nameEn: ませんか (would you like to)
rules.descriptionEn: Politely invites the listener to do something.
rules.exampleJa: お茶を飲みませんか。
rules.exampleEn: Would you like to have tea?

rules.descriptionEn: Plain negative verb form used in casual speech and before other patterns.
rules.exampleJa: 行かない。
rules.exampleEn: I am not going.

rules.descriptionEn: Plain past verb form, also used before nouns and other patterns.
rules.exampleJa: 食べた。
rules.exampleEn: I ate.

rules.descriptionEn: Connects clauses in sequence and feeds many other patterns.
rules.exampleJa: 起きて顔を洗います。
rules.exampleEn: I get up and wash my face.

rules.descriptionEn: Politely asks someone to do something.
rules.exampleJa: 待ってください。
rules.exampleEn: Please wait.

rules.nameEn: ています (ongoing action or state)
rules.descriptionEn: Describes an action in progress or a state that continues.
rules.exampleJa: 本を読んでいます。
rules.exampleEn: I am reading a book.

rules.descriptionEn: Gives or asks for permission.
rules.formation: Verb て + もいいです
rules.exampleJa: 帰ってもいいですか。
rules.exampleEn: May I go home?

rules.nameEn: ないでください (please do not)
rules.descriptionEn: Politely asks someone not to do something.
rules.formation: Verb ない stem + でください
rules.exampleJa: 写真を撮らないでください。
rules.exampleEn: Please do not take photos.

rules.descriptionEn: Expresses the speaker's own wish to do something.
rules.exampleJa: 水が飲みたいです。
rules.exampleEn: I want to drink water.

rules.nameEn: があります / います (there is)
rules.descriptionEn: States existence: あります for things, います for living beings.
rules.formation: Noun + が + あります / います
rules.exampleJa: 机の上に本があります。
rules.exampleEn: There is a book on the desk.

rules.descriptionEn: Expresses liking, where the liked thing takes が.
rules.exampleJa: 音楽が好きです。
rules.exampleEn: I like music.

rules.descriptionEn: Adjectives ending in い that inflect for tense and negation by themselves.
rules.formation: Adjective + です / くない / かった
rules.exampleJa: この本は面白いです。
rules.exampleEn: This book is interesting.

rules.descriptionEn: Adjectives that need な before a noun and use the copula to inflect.
rules.exampleJa: 静かな部屋です。
rules.exampleEn: It is a quiet room.

rules.descriptionEn: Negates an i-adjective by replacing the final vowel.
rules.exampleJa: 高くないです。
rules.exampleEn: It is not expensive.

rules.descriptionEn: Puts an i-adjective into the past.
rules.exampleJa: 楽しかったです。
rules.exampleEn: It was fun.

rules.descriptionEn: Turns an adjective into an adverb describing how an action is done.
rules.formation: i-adjective stem + く; na-adjective + に
rules.exampleJa: 早く歩きます。
rules.exampleEn: I walk quickly.

rules.nameEn: これ / それ / あれ (demonstrative pronouns)
rules.descriptionEn: Points at things near the speaker, near the listener, or away from both.
rules.exampleJa: それは何ですか。
rules.exampleEn: What is that?

rules.nameEn: この / その / あの (demonstrative modifiers)
rules.descriptionEn: Points at a noun near the speaker, listener, or neither.
rules.exampleJa: この本を読みます。
rules.exampleEn: I will read this book.

rules.nameEn: どこ / 何 / 誰 (question words)
rules.descriptionEn: Asks about place, thing, and person.
rules.formation: Question word in the slot being asked about
rules.exampleJa: 誰が来ますか。
rules.exampleEn: Who is coming?

rules.nameEn: いつ / いくら (when, how much)
rules.descriptionEn: Asks about time and price.
rules.formation: Question word in the slot being asked about
rules.exampleJa: いくらですか。
rules.exampleEn: How much is it?

rules.descriptionEn: Asks which one out of a known set.
rules.formation: どの + noun; どちら standalone
rules.exampleJa: どちらが好きですか。
rules.exampleEn: Which do you prefer?

rules.descriptionEn: Counting requires a counter word matched to what is counted.
rules.exampleJa: 本を三冊買いました。
rules.exampleEn: I bought three books.

rules.descriptionEn: Compares two things and says which one is more.
rules.formation: Noun + より + noun + のほうが + adjective
rules.exampleJa: バスより電車のほうが早いです。
rules.exampleEn: The train is faster than the bus.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the top item within a group.
rules.exampleJa: クラスで一番背が高いです。
rules.exampleEn: He is the tallest in the class.

rules.descriptionEn: Says that one action happens before another.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun + の + 前に
rules.exampleJa: 寝る前に歯を磨きます。
rules.exampleEn: I brush my teeth before sleeping.

rules.descriptionEn: Says that one action happens after another.
rules.formation: Verb た form / noun + の + あとで
rules.exampleJa: 食べたあとで散歩します。
rules.exampleEn: I take a walk after eating.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the time at which something else happens.
rules.formation: Clause in modifying form + とき
rules.exampleJa: 子供のとき、京都に住んでいました。
rules.exampleEn: When I was a child I lived in Kyoto.

rules.descriptionEn: Gives a reason, with the reason coming first.
rules.exampleJa: 寒いから窓を閉めます。
rules.exampleEn: I will close the window because it is cold.

rules.descriptionEn: Joins two clauses with contrast in a neutral register.
rules.exampleJa: 高いですが、買います。
rules.exampleEn: It is expensive, but I will buy it.

rules.descriptionEn: Joins clauses with contrast in a softer, more conversational tone.
rules.exampleJa: 行きたいけれど、時間がない。
rules.exampleEn: I want to go, but I have no time.

rules.descriptionEn: Limits something to just that amount or item.
rules.exampleJa: 少しだけ食べました。
rules.exampleEn: I ate only a little.

rules.descriptionEn: States an obligation that cannot be avoided.
rules.formation: Verb ない stem + なければなりません
rules.exampleJa: 薬を飲まなければなりません。
rules.exampleEn: I have to take medicine.

rules.nameEn: なくてもいいです (do not have to)
rules.descriptionEn: States that something is not required.
rules.formation: Verb ない stem + なくてもいいです
rules.exampleJa: 来なくてもいいです。
rules.exampleEn: You do not have to come.

rules.descriptionEn: States ability or possibility.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことができます
rules.exampleJa: 日本語を話すことができます。
rules.exampleEn: I can speak Japanese.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks whether a state continues or has already changed.
rules.exampleJa: もう食べました。
rules.exampleEn: I have already eaten.

rules.nameEn: とても / あまり (very, not very)
rules.descriptionEn: Adjusts degree; あまり pairs with a negative.
rules.exampleJa: あまり高くないです。
rules.exampleEn: It is not very expensive.

rules.descriptionEn: States who does the action with you.
rules.exampleJa: 母と一緒に行きます。
rules.exampleEn: I will go together with my mother.

rules.descriptionEn: Describes a change of state.
rules.formation: Noun / na-adjective + に + なります
rules.exampleJa: 医者になります。
rules.exampleEn: I will become a doctor.

rules.descriptionEn: Describes a change of state with an i-adjective.
rules.formation: Adjective stem + く + なります
rules.exampleJa: 寒くなりました。
rules.exampleEn: It has got cold.

rules.descriptionEn: Says the result holds regardless of the condition.
rules.exampleJa: 雨が降っても行きます。
rules.exampleEn: I will go even if it rains.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a condition whose result follows once it is met.
rules.exampleJa: 駅に着いたら電話します。
rules.exampleEn: I will call when I arrive at the station.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a condition in a neutral or written register.
rules.exampleJa: 安ければ買います。
rules.exampleEn: I will buy it if it is cheap.

rules.nameEn: なら (if it is the case that)
rules.descriptionEn: Takes up a topic the other person raised and responds to it.
rules.exampleJa: 旅行なら京都がいいです。
rules.exampleEn: If you mean travel, Kyoto is good.

rules.descriptionEn: States a result that always follows the condition.
rules.exampleJa: 春になると花が咲きます。
rules.exampleEn: When spring comes, flowers bloom.

rules.descriptionEn: Verb form expressing ability or possibility.
rules.formation: Godan e-stem + る; ichidan + られる
rules.exampleJa: 漢字が読めます。
rules.exampleEn: I can read kanji.

rules.descriptionEn: Plain form expressing intention or a suggestion.
rules.exampleJa: 行こう。
rules.exampleEn: Let us go.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the subject as the one affected by the action.
rules.exampleJa: 先生に褒められました。
rules.exampleEn: I was praised by the teacher.

rules.descriptionEn: Says that someone makes or lets another person act.
rules.exampleJa: 子供に野菜を食べさせます。
rules.exampleEn: I make my child eat vegetables.

rules.descriptionEn: Says the subject was made to do something.
rules.formation: Verb + せられる / させられる
rules.exampleJa: 残業させられました。
rules.exampleEn: I was made to work overtime.

rules.descriptionEn: Blunt command form, common in signs and rough speech.
rules.exampleJa: 早く来い。
rules.exampleEn: Come quickly.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an action done as a favour for someone else.
rules.exampleJa: 友だちに教えてあげました。
rules.exampleEn: I taught my friend as a favour.

rules.nameEn: てくれる (someone does for me)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks an action someone does for the speaker's benefit.
rules.exampleJa: 母が作ってくれました。
rules.exampleEn: My mother made it for me.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an action the speaker receives as a favour.
rules.exampleJa: 先生に見てもらいました。
rules.exampleEn: I had the teacher look at it.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an action done ahead of time and left that way.
rules.exampleJa: 切符を買っておきます。
rules.exampleEn: I will buy the tickets in advance.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks completion, often with regret.
rules.exampleJa: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
rules.exampleEn: I ended up forgetting my homework.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks doing something to see how it goes.
rules.exampleJa: 着てみてもいいですか。
rules.exampleEn: May I try it on?

rules.nameEn: ていく / てくる (direction of change)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks movement away or towards, or a change over time.
rules.formation: Verb て + いく / くる
rules.exampleJa: だんだん暖かくなってきました。
rules.exampleEn: It has gradually got warmer.

rules.nameEn: たことがある (have done before)
rules.descriptionEn: States that the speaker has had an experience at least once.
rules.formation: Verb た form + ことがある
rules.exampleJa: 北海道に行ったことがあります。
rules.exampleEn: I have been to Hokkaido.

rules.descriptionEn: States a firm personal plan.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + つもりだ
rules.exampleJa: 来年留学するつもりです。
rules.exampleEn: I intend to study abroad next year.

rules.descriptionEn: States an intention just decided or being weighed.
rules.exampleJa: 早く寝ようと思います。
rules.exampleEn: I think I will go to bed early.

rules.descriptionEn: States a conclusion the speaker has reason to expect.
rules.exampleJa: 彼は来るはずです。
rules.exampleEn: He should be coming.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks something as a real but uncertain possibility.
rules.formation: Plain form + かもしれない
rules.exampleJa: 雨が降るかもしれません。
rules.exampleEn: It might rain.

rules.descriptionEn: States the speaker's conjecture.
rules.exampleJa: 明日は晴れるだろう。
rules.exampleEn: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

rules.descriptionEn: Reports information heard from elsewhere.
rules.exampleJa: 台風が来るそうです。
rules.exampleEn: I hear a typhoon is coming.

rules.descriptionEn: Describes an impression from what the speaker can see.
rules.formation: Verb stem / adjective stem + そうだ
rules.exampleJa: おいしそうですね。
rules.exampleEn: That looks delicious.

rules.descriptionEn: States an inference based on evidence.
rules.exampleJa: 誰もいないようです。
rules.exampleEn: It seems nobody is here.

rules.descriptionEn: Reports something inferred from outside information.
rules.exampleJa: 店は休みらしいです。
rules.exampleEn: The shop is apparently closed.

rules.descriptionEn: Casual equivalent of ようだ for stating an impression.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + みたいだ
rules.exampleJa: 風邪みたいです。
rules.exampleEn: It seems to be a cold.

rules.descriptionEn: States an obligation in a slightly more conversational register.
rules.formation: Verb ない stem + なくてはいけない
rules.exampleJa: 行かなくてはいけません。
rules.exampleEn: I have to go.

rules.descriptionEn: States a prohibition that applies to the listener.
rules.formation: Verb て + はいけない
rules.exampleJa: ここで泳いではいけません。
rules.exampleEn: You must not swim here.

rules.descriptionEn: Recommends one course of action.
rules.formation: Verb た form + ほうがいい
rules.exampleJa: 休んだほうがいいです。
rules.exampleEn: You had better rest.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks two actions by one person at the same time.
rules.exampleJa: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
rules.exampleEn: I study while listening to music.

rules.descriptionEn: Lists representative actions.
rules.exampleJa: 泳いだり走ったりしました。
rules.exampleEn: I did things like swimming and running.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an action done without doing something else.
rules.exampleJa: 朝ご飯を食べないで出ました。
rules.exampleEn: I left without eating breakfast.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a result that contradicts expectation.
rules.exampleJa: 薬を飲んだのに治りません。
rules.exampleEn: Even though I took medicine, I did not get better.

rules.descriptionEn: Gives a reason in a soft, objective tone.
rules.exampleJa: 用事があるので失礼します。
rules.exampleEn: I have an errand, so please excuse me.

rules.descriptionEn: Stacks up reasons or qualities.
rules.exampleJa: 安いし、近いです。
rules.exampleEn: It is cheap, and it is close.

rules.nameEn: ようになる (come to be able)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a change reaching a new state or ability.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / potential + ようになる
rules.exampleJa: 泳げるようになりました。
rules.exampleEn: I have become able to swim.

rules.nameEn: ようにする (make an effort to)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a deliberate effort or habit.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / ない form + ようにする
rules.exampleJa: 毎日歩くようにしています。
rules.exampleEn: I make a point of walking every day.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the speaker's own decision.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / ない form + ことにする
rules.exampleJa: たばこをやめることにしました。
rules.exampleEn: I decided to quit smoking.

rules.nameEn: ことになる (it has been decided)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a decision made by circumstances or others.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことになる
rules.exampleJa: 来月転勤することになりました。
rules.exampleEn: It has been decided that I will transfer next month.

rules.nameEn: ところだ (just about to, just did)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks the exact stage of an action.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / た form + ところだ
rules.exampleJa: 今出るところです。
rules.exampleEn: I am just about to leave.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks something that happened moments ago.
rules.formation: Verb た form + ばかり
rules.exampleJa: 着いたばかりです。
rules.exampleEn: I have only just arrived.

rules.descriptionEn: A plain-form clause placed directly before a noun to describe it.
rules.exampleJa: 母が作ったケーキ
rules.exampleEn: the cake my mother made

rules.nameEn: やすい / にくい (easy or hard to do)
rules.descriptionEn: Says an action is easy or difficult to perform.
rules.formation: Verb stem + やすい / にくい
rules.exampleJa: この字は読みにくいです。
rules.exampleEn: This character is hard to read.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an amount or degree that goes past what is appropriate.
rules.formation: Verb stem / adjective stem + すぎる
rules.exampleJa: 食べすぎました。
rules.exampleEn: I ate too much.

rules.nameEn: 始める / 終わる (start, finish doing)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks the beginning or end of an action.
rules.formation: Verb stem + 始める / 終わる
rules.exampleJa: 本を読み始めました。
rules.exampleEn: I started reading the book.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an action continued over time.
rules.exampleJa: 三時間走り続けました。
rules.exampleEn: I kept running for three hours.

rules.descriptionEn: Turns a verb into how something is done.
rules.exampleJa: 使い方が分かりません。
rules.exampleEn: I do not know how to use it.

rules.descriptionEn: Describes another person's feelings from their behaviour.
rules.exampleJa: 妹は寒がっています。
rules.exampleEn: My sister is acting cold.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks something that nearly happened.
rules.exampleJa: 転びそうになりました。
rules.exampleEn: I almost fell over.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a window of time in which something else happens.
rules.formation: Noun + の / plain form + 間に
rules.exampleJa: 寝ている間に雨が降りました。
rules.exampleEn: It rained while I was asleep.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a state left unchanged.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + の + まま
rules.exampleJa: 電気をつけたまま寝ました。
rules.exampleEn: I fell asleep with the light left on.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an action beginning suddenly.
rules.exampleJa: 急に泣き出しました。
rules.exampleEn: She suddenly burst into tears.

rules.descriptionEn: Presents the statement as the natural conclusion of what came before.
rules.exampleJa: だから遅れたわけです。
rules.exampleEn: That is why you were late, then.

rules.descriptionEn: States a general truth or recalls a past habit.
rules.exampleJa: 子供はよく転ぶものだ。
rules.exampleEn: Children do fall over a lot.

rules.descriptionEn: States what ought to be done.
rules.exampleJa: 早く謝るべきです。
rules.exampleEn: You should apologise quickly.

rules.descriptionEn: Denies a possibility on the basis of reasoning.
rules.exampleJa: 彼が知っているはずがない。
rules.exampleEn: There is no way he knows.

rules.descriptionEn: States a confident conclusion.
rules.exampleJa: 留守に違いない。
rules.exampleEn: They must be out.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a purpose or a manner to match.
rules.exampleJa: 忘れないようにメモします。
rules.exampleEn: I take notes so that I do not forget.

rules.nameEn: ために (in order to, because of)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a purpose, or a cause in written style.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun + の + ために
rules.exampleJa: 健康のために歩きます。
rules.exampleEn: I walk for my health.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks what something is used for.
rules.exampleJa: この道具は切るのに使います。
rules.exampleEn: This tool is used for cutting.

rules.descriptionEn: Raises an extreme example to make a point.
rules.exampleJa: 水さえ飲めなかった。
rules.exampleEn: I could not even drink water.

rules.nameEn: しかない (nothing but, no choice)
rules.descriptionEn: Limits to one option, often the only one left.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + しかない
rules.exampleJa: 待つしかありません。
rules.exampleEn: There is nothing to do but wait.

rules.descriptionEn: Adds a second, often stronger item.
rules.formation: Noun / plain form + だけでなく
rules.exampleJa: 英語だけでなく中国語も話す。
rules.exampleEn: He speaks not only English but also Chinese.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the degree of a state by comparison.
rules.exampleJa: 泣くほど痛かった。
rules.exampleEn: It hurt enough to make me cry.

rules.descriptionEn: Adds a further item beyond the obvious one.
rules.formation: Noun / plain form + ばかりでなく
rules.exampleJa: 彼ばかりでなく私も悪い。
rules.exampleEn: Not only he but I am also at fault.

rules.descriptionEn: Asks the listener to confirm something half remembered.
rules.exampleJa: 会議は何時だっけ。
rules.exampleEn: What time was the meeting again?

rules.nameEn: てもかまわない (do not mind if)
rules.descriptionEn: Grants permission in a tolerant tone.
rules.formation: Verb て + もかまわない
rules.exampleJa: 遅れてもかまいません。
rules.exampleEn: I do not mind if you are late.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a window that will not last.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + の + うちに
rules.exampleJa: 熱いうちに食べてください。
rules.exampleEn: Please eat it while it is hot.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks something that happens on each occasion.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun + の + たびに
rules.exampleJa: 会うたびに背が伸びている。
rules.exampleEn: He is taller every time we meet.

rules.nameEn: 限り (as far as, as long as)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a limit on the claim being made.
rules.exampleJa: 私が知る限り本当です。
rules.exampleEn: As far as I know, it is true.

rules.nameEn: 代わりに (instead of, in return)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a substitution or an exchange.
rules.formation: Noun + の / plain form + 代わりに
rules.exampleJa: 私の代わりに行ってください。
rules.exampleEn: Please go instead of me.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an agent, a cause, or a variable factor.
rules.exampleJa: 人によって考え方が違う。
rules.exampleEn: Ways of thinking differ from person to person.

rules.nameEn: に対して (towards, in contrast to)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks the target of an attitude, or a contrast.
rules.exampleJa: 客に対して丁寧に話す。
rules.exampleEn: He speaks politely towards customers.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the topic being discussed.
rules.exampleJa: 環境について話しました。
rules.exampleEn: We talked about the environment.

rules.nameEn: として (as, in the role of)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a role or capacity.
rules.exampleJa: 医者として働いています。
rules.exampleEn: I work as a doctor.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the source of reported information.
rules.exampleJa: 天気予報によると雨です。
rules.exampleEn: According to the forecast it will rain.

rules.nameEn: わけがない (there is no way)
rules.descriptionEn: Denies a possibility outright.
rules.exampleJa: そんなことがあるわけがない。
rules.exampleEn: There is no way that happens.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something has the flavour of the noun or quality.
rules.exampleJa: 子供っぽい話し方だ。
rules.exampleEn: It is a childish way of speaking.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something tends to happen.
rules.exampleJa: 忘れがちです。
rules.exampleEn: I tend to forget.

rules.descriptionEn: Says a slight amount of a condition is present.
rules.exampleJa: 風邪気味です。
rules.exampleEn: I have a touch of a cold.

rules.descriptionEn: Compares manner informally.
rules.formation: Noun / plain form + みたいに
rules.exampleJa: 鳥みたいに飛びたい。
rules.exampleEn: I want to fly like a bird.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something shows no sign of happening.
rules.exampleJa: 雨は止みそうもない。
rules.exampleEn: The rain shows no sign of stopping.

rules.nameEn: てはならない (must not, formal)
rules.descriptionEn: States a formal prohibition.
rules.formation: Verb て + はならない
rules.exampleJa: 秘密を漏らしてはならない。
rules.exampleEn: You must not leak the secret.

rules.nameEn: ざるを得ない (cannot help but)
rules.descriptionEn: States something unavoidable in formal style.
rules.formation: Verb ない stem + ざるを得ない
rules.exampleJa: 認めざるを得ない。
rules.exampleEn: I have no choice but to admit it.

rules.nameEn: ように見える (looks as if)
rules.descriptionEn: Reports how something appears.
rules.formation: Plain form + ように見える
rules.exampleJa: 疲れているように見えます。
rules.exampleEn: You look tired.

rules.nameEn: つもりだった (had intended to)
rules.descriptionEn: States an intention that was not carried out.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + つもりだった
rules.exampleJa: 電話するつもりでした。
rules.exampleEn: I had intended to call.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something does not happen despite effort.
rules.exampleJa: なかなか眠れません。
rules.exampleEn: I cannot get to sleep easily.

rules.descriptionEn: States the single sufficient condition.
rules.exampleJa: 時間さえあればできます。
rules.exampleEn: I could do it if only I had time.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks what was found after doing something.
rules.formation: Verb た form + ところ
rules.exampleJa: 調べたところ間違いでした。
rules.exampleEn: Upon checking, it was a mistake.

rules.descriptionEn: Expresses regret about what was not done.
rules.exampleJa: もっと勉強すればよかった。
rules.exampleEn: I should have studied more.

rules.descriptionEn: States a wish about another person's action.
rules.exampleJa: 手伝ってほしいです。
rules.exampleEn: I want you to help me.

rules.descriptionEn: Reports an instruction indirectly.
rules.exampleJa: 静かにするように言われました。
rules.exampleEn: I was told to be quiet.

rules.descriptionEn: Front-loads the speaker's reaction to what follows.
rules.exampleJa: 驚いたことに彼が来た。
rules.exampleEn: To my surprise, he came.

rules.nameEn: にしたがって (in accordance with, as)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a parallel change or compliance.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + にしたがって
rules.exampleJa: 年をとるにしたがって忘れやすくなる。
rules.exampleEn: As you age you forget more easily.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks simultaneity or accompaniment in written style.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + とともに
rules.exampleJa: 成長とともに変わります。
rules.exampleEn: It changes along with growth.

rules.descriptionEn: Credits a good result to a cause.
rules.formation: Noun + の / plain form + おかげで
rules.exampleJa: 君のおかげで助かった。
rules.exampleEn: Thanks to you I was saved.

rules.descriptionEn: Blames a bad result on a cause.
rules.formation: Noun + の / plain form + せいで
rules.exampleJa: 雨のせいで遅れました。
rules.exampleEn: I was late because of the rain.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks simultaneity or concession in written style.
rules.exampleJa: 悪いと知りつつ続けた。
rules.exampleEn: He continued while knowing it was wrong.

rules.nameEn: どうしても〜ない (no matter what)
rules.descriptionEn: Says something cannot be done however hard one tries.
rules.exampleJa: どうしても思い出せない。
rules.exampleEn: I simply cannot remember.

rules.descriptionEn: Excludes one item from a set.
rules.exampleJa: 私以外は全員来ました。
rules.exampleEn: Everyone apart from me came.

rules.descriptionEn: Says an action matches an instruction or model.
rules.formation: Verb た form / noun + の + とおりに
rules.exampleJa: 説明したとおりにやってください。
rules.exampleEn: Please do it just as I explained.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks acting in line with an impulse or state.
rules.exampleJa: 思いのままに書いた。
rules.exampleEn: I wrote as I pleased.

rules.descriptionEn: States a conclusion as beyond doubt.
rules.formation: Plain form + に決まっている
rules.exampleJa: 嘘に決まっている。
rules.exampleEn: It is obviously a lie.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something is unnecessary.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことはない
rules.exampleJa: 心配することはない。
rules.exampleEn: There is no need to worry.

rules.nameEn: わけにはいかない (cannot afford to)
rules.descriptionEn: States that something is not permissible in the circumstances.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + わけにはいかない
rules.exampleJa: 黙っているわけにはいかない。
rules.exampleEn: I cannot just keep quiet.

rules.descriptionEn: Says there is no means available.
rules.exampleJa: 連絡しようがない。
rules.exampleEn: There is no way to get in touch.

rules.descriptionEn: Warns that an undesirable outcome is possible.
rules.exampleJa: 事故になりかねない。
rules.exampleEn: It could well lead to an accident.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something is difficult to do, in formal style.
rules.exampleJa: 信じがたい話です。
rules.exampleEn: It is a hard story to believe.

rules.nameEn: どころではない (in no state to)
rules.descriptionEn: Says the situation rules the action out.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + どころではない
rules.exampleJa: 旅行どころではない。
rules.exampleEn: I am in no position to travel.

rules.descriptionEn: Rejects something emphatically.
rules.exampleJa: 負けるものか。
rules.exampleEn: As if I would lose.

rules.descriptionEn: Adds a further, stronger item.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + ばかりか
rules.exampleJa: 遅刻したばかりか宿題も忘れた。
rules.exampleEn: Not only was he late, he also forgot his homework.

rules.descriptionEn: Adds a second point in the same direction.
rules.exampleJa: 安い上においしい。
rules.exampleEn: It is cheap, and tasty on top of that.

rules.descriptionEn: Widens the scope beyond one case.
rules.exampleJa: 子供に限らず大人も楽しめる。
rules.exampleEn: Not only children but adults can enjoy it.

rules.descriptionEn: Says someone acts while ignoring something.
rules.formation: Noun / plain form + もかまわず
rules.exampleJa: 人目もかまわず泣いた。
rules.exampleEn: She cried without caring who saw.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something proceeds without an element.
rules.exampleJa: 冗談抜きで話そう。
rules.exampleEn: Let us talk with the jokes left out.

rules.descriptionEn: Says the result follows naturally from the reason.
rules.exampleJa: 期待していただけに残念だ。
rules.exampleEn: It is disappointing precisely because I had hoped.

rules.descriptionEn: Offers a reason as an explanation or excuse.
rules.exampleJa: 急いでいたものだから忘れた。
rules.exampleEn: I forgot because I was in a hurry.

rules.nameEn: ことから (from the fact that)
rules.descriptionEn: Draws a conclusion from a stated fact.
rules.exampleJa: 足跡があることから侵入が分かった。
rules.exampleEn: From the footprints we knew of the intrusion.

rules.nameEn: 上で (after doing, on the basis of)
rules.descriptionEn: Says the second step follows the first.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / た form + 上で
rules.exampleJa: 確認した上で返事します。
rules.exampleEn: I will reply after checking.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a formal occasion or moment.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / た form / noun + の + 際に
rules.exampleJa: 出発の際に確認します。
rules.exampleEn: I will check at the time of departure.

rules.nameEn: にあたって (on the occasion of)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks an important juncture in formal style.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun + にあたって
rules.exampleJa: 開会にあたって一言申し上げます。
rules.exampleEn: Let me say a word on the occasion of the opening.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a place, time, or field in formal writing.
rules.exampleJa: 会議は東京において行われる。
rules.exampleEn: The meeting will be held in Tokyo.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a topic in formal style.
rules.exampleJa: この件に関して説明します。
rules.exampleEn: I will explain regarding this matter.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the basis for an action or judgement.
rules.exampleJa: 事実に基づいて書く。
rules.exampleEn: I write based on the facts.

rules.nameEn: に沿って (along, in line with)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks conformity to a line or a policy.
rules.exampleJa: 方針に沿って進める。
rules.exampleEn: We proceed in line with the policy.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a medium or a whole span.
rules.exampleJa: 友人を通じて知りました。
rules.exampleEn: I found out through a friend.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the disputed topic of a discussion.
rules.exampleJa: 税制をめぐって議論が続く。
rules.exampleEn: Debate continues surrounding the tax system.

rules.descriptionEn: Says a distinction does not matter.
rules.exampleJa: 年齢を問わず参加できます。
rules.exampleEn: Anyone can join regardless of age.

rules.descriptionEn: Presents two opposing sides of one thing.
rules.exampleJa: 便利な反面高いです。
rules.exampleEn: It is convenient, but expensive on the other hand.

rules.descriptionEn: Contrasts two simultaneous facts.
rules.exampleJa: 収入は増える一方で支出も増えた。
rules.exampleEn: Income rose while spending also rose.

rules.nameEn: にもかかわらず (in spite of)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a result contrary to expectation, formally.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + にもかかわらず
rules.exampleJa: 雨にもかかわらず出発した。
rules.exampleEn: We set off in spite of the rain.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a contrast with a note of blame.
rules.exampleJa: 知っているくせに黙っていた。
rules.exampleEn: He kept quiet even though he knew.

rules.nameEn: とはいえ (although it is true that)
rules.descriptionEn: Concedes a point before contradicting it.
rules.exampleJa: 安いとはいえ質は悪い。
rules.exampleEn: Cheap though it is, the quality is poor.

rules.nameEn: ものなら (if it were possible)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks an unlikely or wished-for condition.
rules.exampleJa: できるものならやりたい。
rules.exampleEn: I would do it if I possibly could.

rules.nameEn: たらきりがない (there is no end to)
rules.descriptionEn: Says a list could go on forever.
rules.formation: Verb た form + らきりがない
rules.exampleJa: 数えたらきりがない。
rules.exampleEn: There would be no end to counting them.

rules.nameEn: ないことはない (it is not that ... not)
rules.descriptionEn: Softly admits a possibility.
rules.formation: Verb ない form + ことはない
rules.exampleJa: できないことはない。
rules.exampleEn: It is not that it cannot be done.

rules.nameEn: つつある (in the process of)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a change under way, in written style.
rules.exampleJa: 状況は改善しつつある。
rules.exampleEn: The situation is improving.

rules.nameEn: につれて (as, in proportion to)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks two changes moving together.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + につれて
rules.exampleJa: 年をとるにつれて忘れやすくなる。
rules.exampleEn: As one ages one forgets more easily.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a change that comes with another.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + に伴って
rules.exampleJa: 人口増加に伴って問題も増えた。
rules.exampleEn: Problems grew along with the population.

rules.descriptionEn: Sets an element aside for the sake of argument.
rules.exampleJa: 冗談を抜きにして考えよう。
rules.exampleEn: Let us think about it setting jokes aside.

rules.nameEn: 限りでは (as far as ... goes)
rules.descriptionEn: Limits a claim to the available evidence.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / た form + 限りでは
rules.exampleJa: 見た限りでは問題ない。
rules.exampleEn: As far as I could see there is no problem.

rules.nameEn: べきではない (ought not to)
rules.descriptionEn: States what should not be done.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + べきではない
rules.exampleJa: 諦めるべきではない。
rules.exampleEn: You ought not to give up.

rules.nameEn: ようでは (if things are like this)
rules.descriptionEn: Warns about a consequence of the current state.
rules.exampleJa: こんな成績ようでは困る。
rules.exampleEn: If your marks are like this, it is a problem.

rules.nameEn: だけあって (as one would expect)
rules.descriptionEn: Says the result matches a known merit.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + だけあって
rules.exampleJa: プロだけあって上手だ。
rules.exampleEn: He is skilled, as you would expect from a professional.

rules.descriptionEn: Judges something against an expected standard.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + にしては
rules.exampleJa: 初めてにしては上手です。
rules.exampleEn: That is good considering it is your first time.

rules.descriptionEn: Compares a result against a proportion.
rules.formation: Plain form / noun + の + 割に
rules.exampleJa: 値段の割においしい。
rules.exampleEn: It tastes good for the price.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an outcome in written style.
rules.formation: Verb た form / noun + の + 結果
rules.exampleJa: 調査の結果分かった。
rules.exampleEn: It became clear as a result of the survey.

rules.descriptionEn: Regrets a better outcome that was missed.
rules.exampleJa: 早く言えばよかったものを。
rules.exampleEn: If only you had said so sooner.

rules.descriptionEn: Says the next step follows immediately.
rules.exampleJa: 着き次第連絡します。
rules.exampleEn: I will contact you as soon as I arrive.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a regular interval.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + ごとに
rules.exampleJa: 五分ごとに来ます。
rules.exampleEn: It comes every five minutes.

rules.descriptionEn: Concedes a point in written style.
rules.formation: Plain form / adjective + ながらも
rules.exampleJa: 狭いながらも快適な部屋。
rules.exampleEn: A small but comfortable room.

rules.descriptionEn: Qualifies a statement just made.
rules.exampleJa: 留学といっても一か月だけです。
rules.exampleEn: Although I say study abroad, it was only a month.

rules.nameEn: 〜もなにもない (nothing of the sort)
rules.descriptionEn: Denies a claim outright in speech.
rules.exampleJa: 遠慮もなにもない。
rules.exampleEn: There is no question of holding back.

rules.descriptionEn: Says an obstacle did not stop someone.
rules.exampleJa: 嵐をものともせず出港した。
rules.exampleEn: They sailed out undaunted by the storm.

rules.descriptionEn: Says someone acted while disregarding something.
rules.exampleJa: 反対をよそに計画を進めた。
rules.exampleEn: They pushed the plan on, ignoring the objections.

rules.descriptionEn: Says an action happened without a required step.
rules.exampleJa: 許可なしに入れません。
rules.exampleEn: You cannot enter without permission.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something never happened during an action, in written style.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことなく
rules.exampleJa: 休むことなく働いた。
rules.exampleEn: He worked without ever resting.

rules.descriptionEn: Declares one option the best.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + に限る
rules.exampleJa: 夏はビールに限る。
rules.exampleEn: In summer nothing beats beer.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an extreme degree in formal style.
rules.exampleJa: 失礼極まる態度だ。
rules.exampleEn: It is an extremely rude attitude.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks the utmost point of a quality.
rules.exampleJa: 贅沢の極みだ。
rules.exampleEn: It is the height of luxury.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something is unbearable, in formal style.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + に堪えない
rules.exampleJa: 見るに堪えない光景。
rules.exampleEn: A sight one cannot bear to look at.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something consists entirely of one thing.
rules.exampleJa: 黒ずくめの服装。
rules.exampleEn: An outfit entirely in black.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something is smeared with a substance.
rules.exampleJa: 泥まみれになった。
rules.exampleEn: He got covered in mud.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something is riddled with an unwanted thing.
rules.exampleJa: 間違いだらけの文章。
rules.exampleEn: Writing full of mistakes.

rules.nameEn: あまり (out of an excess of)
rules.descriptionEn: Says a strong feeling caused an action.
rules.formation: Noun + の / plain form + あまり
rules.exampleJa: 驚きのあまり声が出なかった。
rules.exampleEn: Out of sheer surprise I could not speak.

rules.descriptionEn: Gives a reason in formal written style.
rules.exampleJa: 未熟ゆえに失敗した。
rules.exampleEn: He failed because of inexperience.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks purpose in formal written style.
rules.exampleJa: 解決すべく努力した。
rules.exampleEn: We made an effort in order to resolve it.

rules.descriptionEn: Rejects a premise informally.
rules.exampleJa: 子供でもあるまいし。
rules.exampleEn: It is not as if you were a child.

rules.nameEn: ではあるまいし (it is not as though)
rules.descriptionEn: Dismisses an assumption in formal speech.
rules.exampleJa: 初心者ではあるまいし。
rules.exampleEn: It is not as though you were a beginner.

rules.descriptionEn: Says the outcome defeated an expectation.
rules.exampleJa: 簡単と思いきや難しかった。
rules.exampleEn: I thought it would be easy, but it was hard.

rules.descriptionEn: Says the second event followed instantly.
rules.exampleJa: 着くや否や雨が降った。
rules.exampleEn: The moment we arrived it rained.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks an immediate consequence in written style.
rules.exampleJa: 座るなり眠った。
rules.exampleEn: He fell asleep as soon as he sat down.

rules.descriptionEn: Says the reverse happens right after each attempt.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + そばから
rules.exampleJa: 片付けるそばから散らかす。
rules.exampleEn: No sooner do I tidy up than it is messy again.

rules.nameEn: ついでに (while one is at it)
rules.descriptionEn: Adds a second errand to a first.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary / た form / noun + の + ついでに
rules.exampleJa: 買い物のついでに寄ります。
rules.exampleEn: I will drop by while I am out shopping.

rules.descriptionEn: States an intense feeling in formal style.
rules.exampleJa: うらやましい限りだ。
rules.exampleEn: I could not be more envious.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something merits an action.
rules.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + に足る
rules.exampleJa: 信頼に足る人物。
rules.exampleEn: A person worthy of trust.

rules.nameEn: までもない (no need to go so far as)
rules.descriptionEn: Says an action is unnecessary.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + までもない
rules.exampleJa: 言うまでもない。
rules.exampleEn: It goes without saying.

rules.nameEn: に越したことはない (nothing better than)
rules.descriptionEn: Says one option is preferable if available.
rules.formation: Plain form + に越したことはない
rules.exampleJa: 安いに越したことはない。
rules.exampleEn: There is nothing better than cheap.

rules.nameEn: では済まない (cannot be settled by)
rules.descriptionEn: Says a measure will not be enough.
rules.formation: Noun / plain form + では済まない
rules.exampleJa: 謝罪では済まない。
rules.exampleEn: An apology will not settle it.

rules.nameEn: なくはない (it is not that there is none)
rules.descriptionEn: Concedes a small amount in a guarded way.
rules.formation: Verb / adjective ない form + はない
rules.exampleJa: 興味がなくはない。
rules.exampleEn: It is not that I have no interest.

rules.descriptionEn: Says a feeling cannot be held back, formally.
rules.exampleJa: 同情を禁じ得ない。
rules.exampleEn: I cannot suppress my sympathy.

rules.descriptionEn: Says something is easy to imagine or guess.
rules.formation: Verb dictionary form + に難くない
rules.exampleJa: 想像するに難くない。
rules.exampleEn: It is not hard to imagine.

rules.descriptionEn: Compares in formal written style, often dismissively.
rules.exampleJa: 私ごとき者には無理です。
rules.exampleEn: It is beyond someone like me.

rules.descriptionEn: Denies even the smallest amount.
rules.exampleJa: 一日たりとも忘れない。
rules.exampleEn: I will not forget for even one day.

rules.nameEn: 〜なりとも (at least, even if only)
rules.descriptionEn: Offers a minimal alternative in formal style.
rules.exampleJa: 少しなりとも役に立ちたい。
rules.exampleEn: I want to help at least a little.

rules.descriptionEn: Says an outcome does not depend on a factor.
rules.formation: Noun + のいかんによらず
rules.exampleJa: 理由のいかんによらず認めない。
rules.exampleEn: It is not accepted regardless of the reason.

rules.nameEn: もさることながら (to say nothing of)
rules.descriptionEn: Adds a second, greater point.
rules.formation: Noun + もさることながら
rules.exampleJa: 味もさることながら見た目も良い。
rules.exampleEn: The taste aside, it also looks good.

rules.descriptionEn: Emphasises complete absence.
rules.exampleJa: 文句ひとつ言わない。
rules.exampleEn: He does not utter a single complaint.

rules.descriptionEn: Says a condition is required before something happens.
rules.exampleJa: 経験してにして初めて分かる。
rules.exampleEn: Only when you experience it do you understand.

rules.nameEn: にあって (in the situation of)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks a special circumstance in formal style.
rules.exampleJa: 非常時にあって冷静だった。
rules.exampleEn: He stayed calm in the emergency.

rules.descriptionEn: Says two factors combined to produce a result.
rules.exampleJa: 天候と相まって混雑した。
rules.exampleEn: Coupled with the weather it got crowded.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks a process gone through, formally.
rules.exampleJa: 審査を経て決まった。
rules.exampleEn: It was decided after passing review.

rules.descriptionEn: Marks strict conformity to a standard.
rules.exampleJa: 実情に即して判断する。
rules.exampleEn: We judge in conformity with the actual situation.

rules.nameEn: を踏まえて (on the basis of)
rules.descriptionEn: Marks the grounds taken into account.
rules.exampleJa: 結果を踏まえて話す。
rules.exampleEn: I speak on the basis of the results.

rules.nameEn: にしても〜にしても (whether ... or)
rules.descriptionEn: Says the result holds in either case.
rules.exampleJa: 行くにしても行かないにしても連絡して。
rules.exampleEn: Contact me whether you go or not.
